title: Move NanoBanana 2 to OpenRouter
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Routes `nanobanana-2` through OpenRouter’s pinned Google Vertex endpoint with fallback disabled.
- Preserves aliases, 1K/2K/4K selection, reasoning controls, 14 references, pricing, EXIF, and content-policy 400 responses.
- Direct 4K generation and 2K editing passed; local alias E2E returned a valid 1024×1024 JPEG in 12.1s with exact billing and a byte-identical cache hit.
- Focused stack verification after syncing `main`: 26/26 Gen image/access tests and 287/287 Enter aliases/pricing tests.
- Accepted product differences: OpenRouter combines text/image prompt tokens, and its image catalog exposes no safety-settings passthrough. Total billing remains exact; OpenRouter’s own content policy still applies.

gist.headline: NanoBanana found a new branch
gist.blurb: NanoBanana 2 now grows through OpenRouter’s pinned Google Vertex route. The fruit is the same: aliases, references, resolution controls, exact billing, and cache hits all made the trip intact.
gist.summary: Routed the nanobanana-2 image model through OpenRouter’s pinned Google Vertex endpoint with fallback disabled while preserving aliases, 1K/2K/4K output selection, reasoning controls, up to 14 references, EXIF, exact billing, caching, and content-policy 400 responses.
gist.impact: NanoBanana 2 users keep the same generation and editing controls—including validated direct 4K generation and 2K edits—now served through the OpenRouter Vertex route with exact billed totals and reliable cached repeats.
gist.visual_concept: Depict NanoBanana 2 as a cozy pixel-art banana-shaped image seed being carefully routed through a garden path between a retro terminal and a small OpenRouter-style gateway sign, with separate 1K, 2K, and 4K fruit crates. Polli, wearing a tiny courier cap, carries the seed toward the gateway while code-plants, reference-picture frames, and a glowing cache jar show that controls and results survived the move.
